problem: Existing 3D referential grounding datasets (ReferIt3D, ScanRefer, SceneVerse) are small, single-source and single-room, use unnatural or LLM-rephrased statements, and lack scene graphs and free-space targets, so they suit real-world navigation poorly. Models trained on them generalize poorly to fine-grained, multi-room scenes.
motivation: Real-world indoor navigation needs robust grounding in scenes with hundreds of objects and fine-grained classes, and with imperfect or invalid language. 3D vision-language data is scarce compared with 2D data. A large dataset with view-independent, minimal, unambiguous statements, dense scene graphs and traversable free space could support robust, interactive navigation agents.
key_idea: Build a very large synthetic 3D vision-language dataset by heuristically generating spatial relation scene graphs and template-based view-independent, unambiguous, minimal referential statements over 3D scans from five real datasets plus Unity scenes, with free-space annotations as extra navigation targets.
insight: Pre-trained SOTA 3D grounding models (MVT 22.5%, 3D-VisTA 28.9%) drop sharply on VLA-3D versus Nr3D (59.5%, 64.2%) and Sr3D (64.5%, 76.4%), showing poor cross-domain generalization to unseen scenes with many fine-grained objects. Failure analysis finds three error types: object classification, language reasoning (target/anchor mix-up), and spatial reasoning (picking same-class distractors). No training or ablation is run on the dataset itself, so its usefulness as training data is not shown.
method: 3D scan processing: Extracts point clouds from PLY vertices (ScanNet, Matterport3D, ARKitScenes) or samples them from meshes (HM3D, Unity, 3RScan). Gets objects and regions from the original semantic meshes, with open-vocabulary class names mapped to NYU40 and NYUv2, plus the top-3 dominant colors per object via color clustering.

Free-space annotation: Computes horizontally traversable free space, chunks it into sub-regions, and gives each sub-region spatial relations to objects so it can be referred to (e.g. 'the space near the table').

Scene graph generation: Uses heuristics on yawed bounding boxes for 8 relation types (above, below, closest, farthest, between (ternary), near, in, on). Relations are generated exhaustively per region, then filtered by semantic class.

Template-based language generation: Builds referential statements from the scene graph, with relation synonyms for variety. Each statement has at least one relation and uses attributes only when needed to disambiguate; statements are view-independent, unambiguous and minimal (Grice's maxim of manner).
Release: Provides the generation code and a visualizer. Includes 7635 scenes, 11.5K regions, 286K objects in 477 classes, 23.5M relations and 9.7M statements.

setting.backbone: MVT and 3D-VisTA (pre-trained checkpoints, evaluated as-is on the dataset)
setting.training_data: Dataset paper; baselines use their original ReferIt3D (Nr3D/Sr3D) training and are not trained on VLA-3D
setting.observation: 3D point clouds with object-level annotations (bounding boxes, classes, colors)
setting.action_space: none (referential object grounding, selecting a target object)
setting.simulator: none (static scans from ScanNet, Matterport3D, HM3D, 3RScan, ARKitScenes, Unity scenes)
setting.privileged: GT object segmentation/boxes and semantic annotations from the scans are used in the grounding task

numbers.extra: Pre-trained checkpoint evaluated directly; not trained on VLA-3D

numbers_note: The paper is a dataset paper; the numbers are baseline accuracies of existing models, since it proposes no new method. The split name for VLA-3D is not stated, so 'test' is assumed.
results: MVT reaches 22.5% and 3D-VisTA 28.9% grounding accuracy on VLA-3D, against 59.5%/64.2% on Nr3D and 64.5%/76.4% on Sr3D. This shows VLA-3D is a challenging benchmark and that current models generalize poorly.
limitations: Statements are template-generated and use only 8 relation types; no LLM augmentation, compound relations, or view-dependent statements yet.
Baselines are only evaluated zero-shot; no training on VLA-3D and no navigation or action evaluation, so the claimed benefit for navigation is untested.
Annotations rely on heuristics and the original scan labels, so semantic noise and class-mapping errors may propagate.
